title: A Phase 1/2, Open-Label Study to Evaluate the Safety and Efficacy of Autologous CD19-specific Chimeric Antigen Receptor T cells (CABA-201) in Subjects with Systemic Sclerosis. summary: Main objective: To evaluate the efficacy of CABA-201 on % predicted FVC at Week 52 in SSc-ILD subjects

interventions.name: Fludarabin Accord 25 mg/ml Konzentrat zur Herstellung einer Injektions- /Infusionslösung

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Able to provide informed consent
2. Able and willing to comply with the applicable contraception requirements:  •	Women of reproductive potential who are heterosexually active must agree to use 1 highly effective method of contraception (e.g., intrauterine device or intrauterine hormone-releasing system, hormone-based contraception or bilateral tubal occlusion) unless the subject has a sterile male partner (e.g., vasectomy with confirmed sterility) or practices sustained abstinence from Screening to a minimum of 52 weeks after the CABA-201 infusion (CTCG, 2024).   Note: Sustained abstinence is an acceptable practice; however, periodic abstinence, the rhythm method, and the withdrawal method are not acceptable methods of contraception. The reliability of sexual abstinence needs to be evaluated in relation to the duration of the clinical trial and the preferred and usual lifestyle of the subject.  •	Sexually active men, both reproductively competent and vasectomized, are required to use a condom until a minimum of 52 weeks after CABA-201 infusion. Men of reproductive potential who participate in heterosexual intercourse and have partner(s) of childbearing potential are required to use condoms with spermicide from Screening until at least 52 weeks after CABA-201 infusion. Males of reproductive potential must also agree not to donate sperm from Screening to at least 52 weeks after the CABA-201 infusion.
3. Age ≥18 and ≤75 years of age.
4. Diagnosis of SSc as defined by the 2013 American College of Rheumatology (ACR)/ European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology (EULAR) classification criteria for SSc
5. [Redacted for CCI]
6. [Redacted for CCI] Intolerance t certain medications
7. On stable background immunomodulatory therapy as follows:  a.	Agent(s) must have been initiated at least 12 weeks prior to Screening and dose must be stable for at least 8 weeks prior to Screening, except for dose reduction due to safety or tolerability concerns.   b.	Currently prescried at least one standard immunomodulatory therapy for the treatment of SSc.
8. Progressive, active SSc
9. mRSS ≥ 15 at Screening
10. HAQ-DI of ≥0.5 OR PtGA for overall SSc activity of ≥ 3 (numeric rating scale from 0-10).
Exclusion criteria:
1. Systemic sclerosis-like illness or a primary diagnosis of rheumatic autoimmune disease other than SSc, including but not limited to rheumatoid arthritis, SLE, polymyositis, dermatomyositis, systemic vasculitis, Sjögren’s syndrome, anti-synthetase syndrome, or mixed connective tissue disease, as determined by the Investigator. Secondary Sjögren’s or scleroderma myopathy and inflammatory myositis is allowed, if the disease is predominantly driven by SSc, at the discretion of the Investigator.
2. Alanine aminotransferase, aspartate aminotransferase, or bilirubin >2 times the upper limit of normal.
3. Documented history of seizures, encephalopathy, or cerebral edema.
4. [redacted for CCI]
5. Subjects who are unable or unwilling to comply with certain medication pause or discontinuation
6. Prior solid organ (heart, liver, kidney, lung) transplant or hematopoietic cell transplant.
7. Known malignancy or a history of malignancy within 5 years, with exception of excised/cured local basal or squamous cell carcinoma of the skin or carcinoma in situ of the uterine cervix.
8. Planned major surgery during the study evaluation period. Subjects should be counseled that elective major surgery will not be permitted for the 52 weeks following CABA-201 infusion.
9. Contraindications to leukapheresis.
10. History of anaphylactic or severe systemic reaction to FLU, CY, or any of their metabolites.
11. Confirmed positive test for human immunodeficiency virus, hepatitis C antibody, hepatitis B surface antigen, or evidence of active or chronic tuberculosis at Screening
12. Autoimmune disorder other than SSc requiring immunosuppressive or immunomodulatory therapies.
13. Any of the following: a. Active infection requiring medical intervention at Screening. b. Clinically significant chronic infection (i.e., osteomyelitis, bronchiectasis, etc.) within 8 weeks prior to Screening (chronic nail infections are allowed). c. Infection requiring hospitalization or treatment with IV anti-infectives not completed at least 4 weeks prior to Screening. d. History of recurrent infection (3 or more of the same type of infection) requiring hospitalization and IV antibiotics over the previous 52 weeks. e. Opportunistic infection requiring hospitalization and IV antimicrobial treatment within 3 years of Screening. f. Viral infection (e.g., herpes zoster, cytomegalovirus, Epstein-Barr virus, etc.) which has not completely resolved at the time of Screening. g. Known history of primary immunodeficiency, splenectomy, or any underlying condition that predisposes the subject to infection.
14. Current alcohol, drug or chemical abuse or a history of such abuse within 1 year before Screening. Stable dose of medicinal marijuana is allowed.
15. Current symptoms of severe, progressive, or uncontrolled renal, hepatic, hematological, gastrointestinal, pulmonary, psychiatric, cardiac, neurological, or cerebral disease.
16. History of evidence of suicidal ideation within the past 6 months or any suicidal behavior within the past 12 months based on a score of 4 or 5 on the Columbia Suicide Rating Scale (C-SSRS) at Screening.
17. [redacted for CCI]
18. Pregnant or lactating woman, or plan to become pregnant within 52 weeks following CABA-201 infusion.
19. Men of reproductive potential who plan to father a child in the 52 weeks following CABA- 201 infusion.
20. Unable or unwilling to comply with protocol.
21. Any condition that, in the opinion of the Investigator or Sponsor, would interfere with the efficacy or safety evaluations of the study intervention or increase safety risk to the subject.
22. [redacted for CCI]
23. HRCT findings consistent with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) or other non– connective tissue disease, interstitial lung disease, including definite usual interstitial pneumonia (UIP) patterns, UIP with significant traction bronchiectasis or end-stage fibrotic lung disease or radiologic evidence of end-stage fibrotic lung disease. NOTE: probable UIP without significant traction bronchiectasis is allowed.
24. [redacted for CCI]
25. [redacted for CCI]
26. [redacted for CCI]
27. Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) > 2
28. Clinical evidence for active aspiration as determined by the Investigator.
